items.title: Fresh off history-making performance, the circus is headed to Mississauga
items.summary: The circus comes to Mississauga this weekend and it’s bringing a just-completed Canadian first along with it. Performing in Toronto — more specifically, Scarborough — this past Friday, the Royal Canadian Circus delivered a history-making aerial moment for those in attendance. Circus officials, in the midst of their 52nd anniversary Canadian tour, said high-flying trapeze performers The Flying Poema “successfully completed Canada’s first-ever quadruple somersault” as the show entered its final weekend of a 10-day run at Scarborough Town Centre. “The extremely rare feat has only been successfully landed by a handful of performers, and following their historic achievement, The Flying Poema will attempt it again during the remaining stops of the tour,” officials with the Royal Canadian Circus said in an email on Tuesday in advance of their arrival in Mississauga for a 10-day stay. Circus to set up in parking lot of Mississauga mall The Royal Canadian Circus sets up from Aug. 21-30 at Dixie Outlet Mall in the city’s east end. The huge event similarly took over the mall’s parking lot for its August 2025 10-day performance. Circus officials said they’re bringing an “all-new 2026 production” to Canada’s seventh-largest city as part of their latest nationwide tour, which also included recent stops in Hamilton, Brampton, Newmarket, Markham and Vaughan. Moving forward, the circus will visit Burlington (Sept. 3-7) following its stay in Mississauga.

items.title: Popular community cafe to close in Mississauga
items.summary: A popular community hub and cafe announced it will close up shop next month in Mississauga. 89, a non-profit fair trade, vegan cafe and community hub, announced they will close their brick-and-mortar location on Sept. 14. 89 said on Instagram. ” The cafe is a social enterprise that sells goods to support its social, cultural and environmental mission. The menu includes a range of espresso drinks, coffee, smoothies, sandwiches and treats. The organization has rallied for support in the past. In 2018, a $50,000 donation helped keep the cafe open. While the physical location at 2520 Eglinton Ave. W. 89 plans to continue its work. Going forward, they will continue to host community programs, workshops and events in venues across Mississauga, they said on Instagram. Programs include art as a tool for social change, climate action, youth leadership, youth and senior connections and job skills. In the past, the cafe opened its doors and provided a free community space to local organizers.

items.title: Maker Pizza Planning Late Summer Opening In Mississauga
items.summary: Maker Pizza, founded by celebrity chef Matty Matheson (of “The Bear” and his cooking show “Munchies”) and his business partner Shlomo Buchler, will open in late August at 181 City Centre Drive in Mississauga, marking its fifth location, according to its website. The brand launched in 2015 with a location on Cameron Street and continued to expand in subsequent years. The Mississauga location will join four existing Maker Pizza shops: Cameron Street, Bayview Avenue and Carlaw Avenue in Toronto, as well as Bathurst Street in Thornhill. ” The shop sells pizza by the slice or the pie, featuring specialty options such as Siena Margherita, Napoli Dynamite, Dr. Pepperoni and Tropic Thunder. The shop also offers dips including creamy garlic, dill ranch and spicy creamy garlic. Other menu items include a variety of wings and garlic fingers. Love our content? Peel police anti-racism plan brings independent oversight to Mississauga, Brampton
items.summary: Peel Regional Police will face independent oversight as it implements recommendations aimed at eliminating racial profiling and systemic discrimination, under a new agreement that will allow disputes to be settled through binding arbitration. The agreement between Peel Regional Police (PRP), the Peel Police Services Board (PPSB) and the Ontario Human Rights Commission (OHRC) establishes an independent process to verify whether the recommendations are being implemented and resolve disagreements between the three parties. The recommendations are the result of a Human Rights Project launched by the three organizations in 2020 to identify and address systemic racism in Peel policing. The project included consultations with Black, Indigenous and other racialized communities, with initial recommendations released in 2023. Those recommendations were based on seven principles developed by the OHRC and cover areas including acknowledging systemic racism, community engagement, policy changes, accountability, organizational change and data collection. Peel police has since been working to implement the recommendations, but the new agreement establishes an additional layer of oversight to determine whether the work is actually being carried out. Under the agreement, PRP, the police board and the OHRC will jointly select an independent verifier, with support from the community-based Anti-Racism Advisory Committee. The verifier will assess the implementation of the recommendations. If the three organizations disagree over how a recommendation should be interpreted or whether it has been properly implemented, the dispute can be sent to binding arbitration.

items.title: 2 online child luring police investigations lead to multiple charges for Mississauga man
items.summary: A Mississauga man faces multiple charges in connection with two online child sexual abuse investigations conducted by different police forces. York Regional Police said on Tuesday that investigators with the police agency’s Internet Child Exploitation unit laid a number of child sexual abuse and exploitation material charges as part of an ongoing investigation. Police said their probe began in September 2025 when officers started looking into a suspect who was using an online platform to arrange meetings with youths he believed were under the age of 16 for the purpose of committing sexual offences. “Over the span of seven months, the suspect continued to send messages using numerous aliases including ‘Scanner’, ‘Competentist’, ‘James Thomas’, ‘JP T’ and ‘Confessionator’,” York police said in a news release issued Tuesday. Investigators in York were then notified in May by Ontario Provincial Police who were investigating “similar allegations involving the same suspect and motive,” police said. A man was arrested in June in relation to both investigations. John Thompson, 52, of Mississauga, is charged with: John Thompson, 52, of Mississauga.

items.title: Crews Finish Twin Tunnels Linking Crosstown LRT Extension Toward Mississauga and Pearson Airport
items.summary: According to INsauga, Metrolinx says crews have finished tunnelling on twin 500-metre tunnels running between Jane Street and Mount Dennis Station in Toronto, connecting the Eglinton Crosstown West Extension to the existing Line 5 Eglinton line. INsauga reports the underground work began in February and took roughly six months to complete, marking what project leaders called a critical milestone for the transit expansion. The extension will carry Line 5 Eglinton farther west to bring rapid transit service to Etobicoke and Mississauga, and is expected to eventually reach north from the Mississauga-Toronto border toward Toronto Pearson Airport. INsauga notes the provincial government has said the completed extension will help reduce gridlock and connect nearly 70,000 commuters to jobs across the Greater Toronto Area. Ontario Premier Doug Ford said earlier this summer that the government is making what he called historic investments in the largest public transit expansion in North America to support commuters and fight gridlock.

items.title: York Police Say Mississauga Man's Alleged Online Luring Scheme Spanned Two Separate Investigations
items.summary: According to a York Regional Police release, a 52-year-old Mississauga man has been charged in connection with a child luring investigation involving youths under 16. Police say the investigation began last September after they identified a man allegedly using an online platform to arrange meetings with youths he believed were under 16 for the purpose of committing sexual offences. According to police, the Ontario Provincial Police notified York investigators in May 2026 that they were looking into similar allegations involving the same suspect and motive, and the man was charged in June 2026 in connection with both investigations. Investigators have released a photograph of the accused because they believe there may be additional victims who haven't yet come forward. Police are asking anyone with information to contact York Regional Police at 1-866-876-5423, extension 7078.

items.title: New First Aid and Aquatic Leadership Courses Headline Mississauga's Fall Recreation Lineup
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, city residents can now register for Mississauga's fall recreation programs through Active Mississauga, with in-person registration also available at community centres during service desk hours. The lineup includes Swim for Life lessons, which build swimming and water-safety skills through step-by-step instruction for different ages and skill levels, along with aquatic leadership courses meant to give youth and young adults a pathway toward careers such as lifeguarding and swim instruction. Mississauga.com reports a new Intermediate First Aid course, formerly known as Standard First Aid, is being offered this fall and covers how to respond to emergencies including allergic reactions, strokes, burns, fractures, seizures, diabetic emergencies and environmental injuries. That course also includes CPR-C and AED certification, which the city notes is a prerequisite for the more advanced Bronze Cross certification. The city is also offering a range of preschool programs guided by the HIGH FIVE quality standard, according to Mississauga.com.

items.title: 141 New Units Proposed for Three Modular Towers on Ninth Line in Mississauga
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, the City of Mississauga is reviewing a proposal from Mattamy Homes for three modular six-storey apartment buildings at 6344 Ninth Line, just south of Doug Leavens Boulevard. Mississauga.com reports the three towers would together add 141 units to the site. The application asks the city to change the zoning bylaw currently in place so the development can go ahead. According to the report, the proposal also includes additional landscape and public realm enhancements planned around the perimeter of the property. Mississauga.com notes a public meeting on the application has been scheduled for September 21, giving residents a chance to weigh in before the city makes a decision.

items.title: Motorcyclist seriously injured in Hwy. 401 crash in Mississauga
items.summary: A motorcyclist has been rushed to hospital after a crash with a vehicle on Highway 401 in Mississauga. m. Monday. A 53-year-old man was taken to hospital with serious, life-threatening injuries. It’s unknown whether anyone else was injured in the crash. The eastbound express lanes were closed from Winston Churchill to Mavis Road for several hours and the investigation is still ongoing.

items.title: City Reminds Homeowners That Backyard Projects May Require a Tree Permit First
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, residents planning a backyard project such as installing a pool, building a deck or removing a tree should first check whether the work requires a tree permit. The city says trees on both private and public property are protected under Mississauga's tree protection by-laws, which were updated in 2022 to ensure trees across the city are managed responsibly. Checking before cutting can help residents avoid fines, delays and unexpected costs, according to the city, while also protecting Mississauga's broader urban forest. City officials note that healthy trees do more than improve the look of a neighbourhood, since they also provide shade, improve air quality, absorb rainwater and help reduce the effects of extreme heat. As Mississauga experiences hotter summers and more extreme weather, the city says protecting its tree canopy helps keep neighbourhoods cooler, healthier and more resilient.
